builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AutoPI: Taxonomy-Guided Adaptive Red Teaming for Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
summary: AutoPI replaces the fixed attack templates in benchmarks such as AgentDojo and IPI Arena with a taxonomy-guided attacker LLM that generates one injection per sub-technique and iteratively rewrites failures using an LLM judge. It costs inference calls to three models (attacker, target, judge) per scenario, which on API pricing is modest but scales with taxonomy size and retry rounds, and it adds an external taxonomy (PIAtlas) as a maintenance dependency. It can fail when the taxonomy itself is incomplete or stale, since coverage is measured only against known classes, and LLM-judge false positives can overstate both ASR and coverage, leading to misplaced confidence in hardening decisions.
rationale: A training-free, black-box, API-driven red teamer that plugs into existing agent security benchmarks fits constrained infrastructure directly and improves evaluation coverage, which is the metric that matters for hardening production agents against prompt injection.

claims.statement: AutoPI replaces the fixed attack templates in benchmarks such as AgentDojo and IPI Arena with a taxonomy-guided attacker LLM that generates one injection per sub-technique and iteratively rewrites failures using an LLM judge. It costs inference calls to three models (attacker, target, judge) per scenario, which on API pricing is modest but scales with taxonomy size and retry rounds, and it adds an external taxonomy (PIAtlas) as a maintenance dependency. It can fail when the taxonomy itself is incomplete or stale, since coverage is measured only against known classes, and LLM-judge false positives can overstate both ASR and coverage, leading to misplaced confidence in hardening decisions.

On AgentDojo, AutoPI achieves successful injections in all six taxonomy classes and over 90% of techniques against Qwen3.6-35B; against Claude Haiku 5.5 it reports 20-50% higher ASR and 25-400% higher class-level coverage than recent state-of-the-art adaptive red teamers, with no training.
